question.worked_solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

- To find the slope of the line $8x-2y=-2,$ we convert to slope-intercept form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-2y & =-2 \\ -2y & =-8x-2 \\ 2y & =8x+2 \\ y & =4x+1\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $4.$

- To find the slope of the line $kx-5y=15,$ we convert to slope-intercept form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kx-5y & =15 \\ -5y & =-kx+15 \\ 5y & =kx-15 \\ y & =\frac{k}{5}x-3\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $\frac{k}{5}.$

Since the slopes of the two lines must be equal, we must have $\frac{k}{5}=4.$ We solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k}{5} & =4 \\ k & =20\end{aligned}
$$
